::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 3d [1888]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Girton College Cambridge, Yonge IV 4
:::

Dear[Mr Innes](people/person_744.qmd),

People are continually writing in the Autumn to ask me to tell them of cheap easy dramas to be acted by their pupils - gentle or simple. I have just had to decline two such plays for the [Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd) because I do not think they suit in a magazine and I have no room but I do believe that to published them in a very cheap form at so much per dozen copies in good time before Christmas would answer well.

One is Eastern, written for Bible class boys by [Miss Wood](people/person_1550.qmd), Elmwood, Bromley Road, Beckenham, the same who made the grand pictorial map of Palestine.  It has been acted by them and I know of many people who want such things - If you would write to her she would send it.

The other is drawing room - founded on the White Cat, and is by Miss [Constance Prevost](people/person_1207.qmd)[^1], Abbey Grange[,] Street, Somerset. She is a grand-niece of [Mr Keble](people/person_798.qmd) and of considerable ability

Yours truly 
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: This play was published in Prevost's *Terra Cotta Plays* (1888).
